text:
The story around Matvei Michkov this month has had little to do with his stat line. A report that the 21-year-old wanted out of Philadelphia set off a week of trade talk; NBC Sports Philadelphia's source said the Flyers were not aware of any such desire, and several outlets have since reported the team is not trading him. Rick Tocchet told PhillyVoice the Flyers handled the noise "really well," while acknowledging it is there.

On the ice, he is having a breakout: 16:28 a night, up from 14:50, on for 75% of the power play, and 17 points in 23 games. Our numbers see two kinds of luck pulling in opposite directions. His 11 goals come on 6.3 expected, a 31% shooting rate that will not last. But the Flyers have scored 8.7 fewer goals than their chances deserve with him on the ice, which has quietly cost him assists.

He comes in on a four-game point streak, and his own chances are up to 0.99 expected goals per 60. The finishing will cool; the role and the chances look real.
headline: Matvei Michkov, the noise and the numbers
